chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil, may Allah have mercy on him, narrated to us. He said: Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab narrated to me. He said: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated to us. He said: Mu'awiya ibn Wahb narrated to us. He said: I heard Aba Abdillah al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, saying:

Seek knowledge and adorn it with forbearance and dignity. Humble yourselves to the one you are teaching knowledge to, and humble yourselves to the one from whom you sought knowledge. Do not be tyrannical scholars, lest your faults wash away your truth.

key_terms.الْحِلْمِ: forbearance — patience and self-restraint in the face of provocation
key_terms.الْوَقَارِ: dignity/piety — composed demeanor befitting a person of knowledge
key_terms.عُلَمَاءَ جَبَّارِينَ: tyrannical scholars — learned individuals who use knowledge for domination rather than guidance

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq say about the etiquette of seeking and teaching knowledge?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq instructs his followers on the proper etiquette of knowledge. He commands them to seek knowledge and accompany it with forbearance and dignity. He emphasizes mutual humility: scholars must be humble both toward their students and toward their own teachers. The warning against being tyrannical scholars underscores that arrogance and oppressive behavior in learned people can nullify the value of what truth they possess.
word_analysis: may He have mercy on him

en.bilal-muhammad: Muhammad b. Musa b. al-Mutawakkil (rh) narrated to us. He said: `Abdullah b. Ja`far al-Himyari narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. al-Husayn b. Abi’l Khattab narrated to me. He said: Al-Hasan b. Mahbub narrated to us. He said: Mu`awiya b. Wahb narrated to us. He said: I heard Aba `Abdillah al-Sadiq (as) say:

Seek knowledge and adorn it with forbearance and piety. Humble yourself to the one you are teaching knowledge to and humble yourself to the one you sought for knowledge. Do not be tyrannical scholars lest your faults wash away your truth.
